title: Performance analysis of a stencil code using modern C++
problem: Evaluating multiple C++ shared memory programming models for their ability to efficiently express and execute stencil computations like the power method, with varying tradeoffs between ease of expression and runtime performance.
motivation: HPC developers need guidance on which modern C++ programming paradigms provide the best balance between code expressiveness and computational performance for iterative stencil algorithms.
method: The researchers implemented the power method algorithm (a stencil code that updates grid values based on neighboring cells) using several different modern C++ shared memory programming models, which are different ways to write parallel code where multiple threads work with shared memory. For each implementation, they benchmarked both the ease of expressing the algorithm in code and the computational performance, revealing the practical tradeoffs between different approaches.
key_novelty: This work compares different modern C++ shared memory programming models (ways of writing parallel code where threads access shared data) to reveal which approach best balances ease of coding with runtime speed for stencil algorithms.
contributions: Comparative analysis of multiple C++ shared memory programming models for stencil computations
Implementations of the power method algorithm using diverse modern C++ techniques
Empirical performance evaluation and expressiveness assessment across approaches
Guidance for selecting appropriate C++ programming models based on performance-expressiveness tradeoffs
baselines: multiple C++ shared memory programming models
limitations: Limited to shared memory parallelism; distributed memory and accelerator-based approaches are not discussed.
primary_theme: C++ shared memory parallelism for stencil codes
